Counsel for Revisionist :- Sandeep Kumar Srivastava

Hon'ble Subhash Vidyarthi,J.

1. Heard Sri Sandeep Kumar Srivastava, the learned counsel for the revisionist, Sri Akhilesh Kumar Vyas, the learned A.G.A appearing on behalf of the State and perused the record.
2.
The learned A.G.A states that information of the present revision has been delivered to the complainant but no body has put in appearance to opposed the revision on behalf of the complainant.

3. The instant criminal revision has been filed under Section 102 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection) Act, 2015, challenging the validity of order dated 28.08.2023 passed by the Juvenile Justice Board rejecting bail application of the applicant and the judgment and order dated 04.12.2023 passed by the Additional Session Judge/ Special Judge (POCSO Act)- I, Raebareli,
dismissing the Criminal Appeal No. 53/2023 (Child Delinquent 'A' vs. State of U.P.) arising out of F.I.R No. 112/2023, under Sections 363, 366, 376(3), 352, 342, 504, 506, 323 I.P.C. and Section 3(2)5 of SC/ST and 5/6 of POCSO Act, Police Station -Dalmau, District Raebareli filed by the revisionist against rejection of his bail application.

sentences.text: In the F.I.R No. 112 of 2023 lodged on 10.05.2023, the complainant had alleged that when his two daughters had gone to attend the call of nature at about 07:00 pm on 09.05.2023, the applicant caught hold of her elder daughter and started doing obscene activities with her and took her to his home by threatening her.
His younger daughter gave information of this incident at home and thereafter the complainant's daughter was recovered by the police from the house of the applicant.
5. In the statement of the victim recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C, she alleged that the applicant had forcibly taken her away to his home.

She stated that the applicant's house is about half and one kilometer away from the place of occurrence and she has raised a hue and cry but no person was present on the way and nobody came to save her.
The applicant forcibly raped her inside his house.
6. The victim gave a similar statement before the doctor, who had conducted her medico legal examination but no mark of injury or sign of use of force was found on any part of the victim's body.

7. In the affidavit filed in support of the bail application, it has been stated that the applicant is an innocent person, he has been falsely implicated in the present case and he has no criminal history.

8. It is mentioned in the order dated 28.08.2023 passed by the Juvenile Justice Board, that the applicant had been held hostage in the house of the complainant, which raises a doubt against the allegation that the victim was recovered from the house of the applicant where he had raped her.

9. Keeping in view the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case, coupled with the fact that the medico legal examination report of the victim mentions no sign of use of force or any mark of injury on the body of the victim and that the applicant is a juvenile having no criminal history, I am of the view that the instant revision is allowed.

The impugned order dated order dated 28.08.2023 passed by the Juvenile Justice Board rejecting the bail application of the applicant and the judgment and order dated 04.12.2023 passed by the Additional Session Judge/ Special Judge (POCSO Act)- I,
Raebareli, dismissing the Criminal Appeal No. 53/2023 (Child Delinquent 'A' vs. State of U.P.)
arising out of F.I.R No. 112/2023, under Sections 363, 366, 376(3), 352, 342, 504, 506, 323 I.P.C.
and Section 3(2)5 of SC/ST and 5/6 of POCSO Act, Police Station -Dalmau, District Raebareli are hereby set aside.
10. Let the revisionist- Juvenile Delinquent A Thru.

(ii) natural guardian will further furnish an undertaking to the effect that the juvenile will pursue his study at the appropriate level which he would be encouraged to do.
(iii) juvenile accompanied by his natural guardian, will report to the Probation Officer on the first working day of every calendar month.
The D.P.O. shall maintain a diary recording their attendance.

(iv) The District Probation Officer will keep strict vigil on the activities of the juvenile and regularly draw up his social investigation report that would be submitted to the Juvenile Justice Board, Raebareli.
